Subject: Post-call: Redwood TCO recap & next steps

Hi Laura — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the cost levers we discussed, and proposed next steps.

Summary of pain points:
- High token bill for summary/assistant flows (you mentioned ~100M tokens/month expected).
- Unpredictable tail-latency causing UX degradation on customer-facing flows.
- Procurement needs a clear TCO/ROI for FY27 to justify any committed spend.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce per-conversation token cost by ~40% within three months for the assistant product.
- Keep 95th percentile latency under ~300ms for common flows.
- Validate predictable monthly spend at or below your target number (see question below).

Key levers discussed (TCO-focused):
1) Model selection & token economics: moving high-volume assistant traffic to a quantized, slightly smaller variant can reduce per-token compute cost ~25–35% while keeping quality acceptable for templated responses.
2) Batching & dynamic batching: continuous batching during peak windows increases GPU utilization and reduces per-token compute. For your workload shape we estimate ~15% compute savings from improved batching.
3) KV/prefix caching: reuse cached encodings for repeated system prompts and common prefixes to avoid re-encoding ~30% of tokens for some flows.
4) Hybrid routing & fallbacks: route low-priority or bulk requests to cheaper model variants during bursts to avoid expensive autoscaling.
5) Dedicated/reserved capacity: committing to Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput can significantly lower unit cost versus on-demand.

Estimate & ROI framing (very rough):
- Current spend (as discussed on the call): ~$45k/month.
- Pro-forma with levers (model mix + batching + caching + partial reservation): $28k–$32k/month (~28–38% savings).
- Engineering effort to implement: ~2–3 sprints (6–8 engineer-weeks) as a one-time cost.

Attachments (included):
- redwood_tco_onepager.pdf (one-pager with assumptions and scenario table)
- sample_estimate_acme.xlsx (workbook with token math & scenario models)

Requested next steps:
- Can you confirm the procurement-approved target budget for FY27 (you mentioned a constrained range on the call)?
- Please share a sample week of logs (anonymized) with token counts and latency percentiles so we can run a PS estimate — Vivek and I will provide a simple CSV/JSON template.
- Schedule a 60-min deep-dive with your infra + procurement teams. Suggested windows: Tue 8/18 10:00am PT or Wed 8/19 9:00am PT.

Thanks — appreciate the candid conversation and the clear priorities. Ill follow up once I have the template and a calendar invite.

Best,

Laura — great, thanks for the quick reply and the budget clarity. Short answers and next steps below.

- Yes: the pro-forma I shared is based on ~50% of peak on reserved Dedicated capacity. We will produce three scenarios for the workbook: 0% reserved (on-demand), 50% reserved, and 75% reserved.
- We will model an accelerated quantized variant for the high-volume assistant paths and keep the high-quality variant for edge cases (this is where the ~25–35% per-token compute savings come from in the scenarios).
- Wed 8/19 9:00am PT is confirmed for the deep-dive. Ill send a calendar invite to Sanjay and your procurement POC once the logs arrive.

Vivek — action items for us before Wed: 
- Share the CSV/JSON template for logs ingestion and a short runbook for customers to redact/format sample data. (Ill send the template in a separate internal email/attachment.)
- Produce the cost-model update with the three reservation scenarios and a short sensitivity table showing break-even points vs. current spend.

Laura — expect the logs by EOD Mon; Vivek and I will have the initial estimate back to you 24–36 hours after we ingest the sample logs, and we’ll bring a recommended rollout plan (canary -> 100% over ~4 weeks) to the deep-dive.
